name: Median Cleft of the Upper Lip and Maxilla
aliases: Median Cleft Lip and Maxillary Cleft
Midline Cleft of the Upper Lip and Maxilla

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Median Cleft Lip and Maxilla

criteria.description: Presence of a midline cleft of the upper lip extending through the philtrum
Midline cleft or defect involving the maxillary bone
Associated midline nasal deformity or clefting
Exclusion of other syndromic causes of midline facial clefts

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of midline cleft of the upper lip and maxillary bone defects with exclusion of other syndromic conditions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging to assess extent of maxillary involvement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Midline cleft of the upper lip
pathognomonic.notes: Distinctive midline separation of the upper lip
searchTerms: split or gap in center of upper lip
notch or opening in upper lip middle

pathognomonic.notes: Bony defect in the midline of the maxilla
searchTerms: gap in upper jaw bone center

pathognomonic.notes: Nasal cleft or bifid nasal tip

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties due to oral cleft
searchTerms: feeding problems due to lip cleft

common.symptomName: Dental anomalies including missing or malformed teeth
searchTerms: teeth that are malformed or absent

occasional.notes: Eustachian tube dysfunction secondary to cleft
Due to facial appearance and speech difficulties
Reported in some cases without other syndromic features

rare.symptomName: Associated brain midline anomalies (e.g., holoprosencephaly spectrum)

rare.notes: Occasionally reported in association with brain anomalies
May occur but less common than isolated lip and maxillary cleft
searchTerms: split or hole in the roof of mouth

imaging: CT scan demonstrating midline maxillary bone cleft
MRI brain to exclude associated midline brain anomalies
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
Genetic testing to exclude syndromic causes such as holoprosencephaly-related genes
other: Clinical examination revealing midline facial clefting

redFlags: Presence of neurological deficits or seizures
Signs of airway obstruction or respiratory distress
Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties
references: Orphanet: Median cleft of the upper lip and maxilla, ORPHA:141239
